name: SPI Mode Reference
intro: Shows what each SPI mode means (mode = 2·CPOL + CPHA, the Motorola definition used by Linux and Arduino): the idle clock level, the edge data is sampled and shifted on, a timing diagram of one byte, how each MCU family and SDK spells the setting, and the modes common parts accept.
usage: Give mode as all, 0, 1, 2 or 3, an optional part-name filter (device), and optionally a MOSI and MISO byte in hex plus bit order (msb or lsb) for the diagram. Returns CPOL, CPHA, idle level, sample and shift edges, the register/constant spelling for Linux, Arduino, ESP-IDF, Zephyr, STM32, AVR, PIC, SAM, TI and NXP, and the matching parts with the modes their datasheets allow. result.drawing holds the bit sequences the diagram is drawn from.
sources: Motorola/Freescale SPI Block Guide V03.06 (S12SPIV3), CPOL/CPHA definition
ST RM0090 §28.3 (SPI_CR1 CPOL/CPHA), Microchip PIC18 MSSP (CKP/CKE), Atmel SAM3X SPI_CSR (NCPHA), TI MSP430 eUSCI (UCCKPH)
Part datasheets for the device modes (Analog Devices ADXL345, Bosch BME280, Maxim MAX31855, ST LIS3DH, Winbond W25Q128 and others)
